position_description: Conserved octameric palindrome in the -10 region of the atpB promoter; atpB promoter lacks a conserved -35 motif
experimental_evidence: chimeric promoter::uidA(GUS) chloroplast transformation; GUS transcript abundance + in vivo transcription; deletion analysis
key_finding: The atpB promoter has a TATAATAT -10 octamer palindrome but no conserved -35, defining a distinct promoter type from the sigma70-like 16S promoter.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
notes: Octamer conserved in some other C. reinhardtii chloroplast promoters per abstract.

position_description: 16S rRNA gene promoter resembles bacterial sigma70 type with typical -10 and -35 elements
sequence_source_location: not reported (sequence not given in abstract)
experimental_evidence: chimeric promoter::uidA chloroplast transformation; deletion analysis
key_finding: The 16S rRNA promoter is a bacterial sigma70-type (PEP) promoter with both -10 and -35 boxes, structurally distinct from atpB.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
notes: Exact -10/-35 sequences not stated in abstract; do not record sequence.

position_description: Maximum atpB promoter activity requires ~22 bp upstream and ~60 bp downstream of the transcription start site
experimental_evidence: deletion analysis of promoter fragments in vivo
key_finding: atpB promoter needs only ~22 bp upstream of TSS plus downstream sequence for full activity.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
notes: Downstream requirement consistent with promoter-proximal determinants.

position_description: 22 bp upstream of the atpB:GUS transcript 5' end is sufficient to confer wild-type promoter activity; transcription begins at the native start site
experimental_evidence: stable chloroplast transformation (biolistic); RNA blot; in vivo run-on transcription
key_finding: atpA and atpB promoters are fully functional when fused to a foreign gene at an alien locus; 22 bp upstream of atpB TSS gives WT activity.
notes: Foundational in vivo chloroplast promoter assay in Chlamydomonas.

position_description: rbcL promoter directs rbcL:GUS transcription at only ~1% of the expected rate, implying additional features are needed for optimal activity
experimental_evidence: stable chloroplast transformation; RNA blot; in vivo run-on
key_finding: The basic rbcL promoter alone is very weak (~1%), unlike atpA/atpB, indicating extra downstream determinants.
notes: Followed up by Klein 1994 remote element.

position_description: Basic rbcL promoter lies within positions -18 to +63 (TSS = +1); a reporter with only the basic promoter is transcribed at only 1-15% of the endogenous rbcL rate
experimental_evidence: chimeric rbcL::uidA chloroplast transformation; relative in vivo transcription rates
key_finding: The rbcL basic promoter (-18 to +63) is weak alone; full activity needs sequences extending to +170 or beyond.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

position_description: A reporter containing rbcL sequences to +170 or beyond is transcribed at about the endogenous rbcL rate; a downstream (transcribed) element enhances promoter activity
experimental_evidence: chimeric rbcL::uidA chloroplast transformation; in vivo transcription
key_finding: A remote, downstream sequence element (around/beyond +170) enhances rbcL promoter activity ~10-100 fold.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
notes: Later reinterpreted partly as RNA stability (Salvador 2004).

position_description: Deleting the rbcL 5'UTR to +36, altering the first 36 bp, and adding 5 bp between 5'UTR and the basic promoter element at position -10 did not abolish transcription
experimental_evidence: deletion/mutational analysis with uidA(GUS); transcription assays
key_finding: Apparent loss of rbcL 'promoter' activity on 5'UTR deletion is largely due to transcript instability, not loss of transcription; a basic promoter element sits near -10.
notes: Reconciles Blowers 1990/Klein 1994 with RNA-stability role of rbcL 5'UTR.

position_description: A Shine-Dalgarno consensus sequence within the psbA 5'UTR is required for ribosome association and translation
experimental_evidence: site-directed mutagenesis of chloroplast psbA mRNA in vivo
key_finding: psbA translation requires an SD sequence (ribosome binding) plus an upstream structured attenuator element.

position_description: A second element upstream of and adjacent to the SD sequence maps to the message-specific protein binding site and acts as a translational attenuator; secondary structure is required
experimental_evidence: site-directed mutagenesis affecting secondary structure; in vivo translation
key_finding: A structured element upstream of the SD acts as an attenuator overcome for translational activation, likely light-regulated.

position_description: Binding of nuclear-encoded proteins protects a 36-base RNA fragment containing a stem-loop located upstream of the ribosome binding site
experimental_evidence: RNA-protein binding/footprint; correlation with translation in light/dark
key_finding: Light-regulated nuclear-encoded proteins bind a 36-nt psbA leader stem-loop upstream of the RBS and correlate with translation.

position_description: Processing occurs just upstream of a consensus SD sequence and removes 54 nt from the 5' terminus, including a previously identified stem-loop element
experimental_evidence: primer-based 5'-end mapping; mutants blocking translation; in vitro binding
key_finding: psbA 5'UTR is processed (-54 nt) upstream of the SD; processing is coupled to ribosome association/translation.

position_description: Expression of a reporter fused to the psbC 5' nontranslated leader requires wild-type F34 and F64; a point mutation in the leader suppresses the F34 requirement
experimental_evidence: reporter fusion chloroplast transformation; point mutation; in vitro RNA-protein cross-linking
key_finding: psbC 5'UTR mediates translational dependence on two nuclear loci (F34/F64); an ~46-kDa AU-rich-binding protein is implicated.

position_description: A 97-nt region in the middle of the psbC 5'UTR, ~236 nt upstream of the GUG initiation codon, is required for translation initiation
experimental_evidence: in vivo pulse labeling; chimeric reporter; suppressor genetics
key_finding: A distal 97-nt psbC 5'UTR element acts as a translational activator through nuclear TBC1/TBC3.

position_description: Two regions (central leader and near the initiation codon) are important for translation; the 5'-most 93 nt are required for WT transcription/mRNA stabilization
experimental_evidence: series of site-directed mutations; reporter in WT vs tbc mutant backgrounds
key_finding: The 547-nt psbC leader contains separable translation elements (TBC1 central + initiation-region targets; TBC2 3' targets) and a 5' stability region.

position_description: The 74-nt psbD leader includes a target site for psbD RNA degradation in the absence of NAC2; primary cleavage sites mapped
experimental_evidence: chimeric psbD leader::reporter in WT vs nac2-26; in vitro lysate degradation; cleavage mapping
key_finding: The short psbD 5' leader confers NAC2-dependent stability; loss of a 47-kDa leader-binding protein correlates with instability.

position_description: Two major stability determinants: within the first 12 nt at the 5' end and near position -30 relative to the AUG
experimental_evidence: site-directed mutagenesis + biolistic transformation
key_finding: psbD mRNA stability depends on the extreme 5' end and a ~-30 element; two further elements affect translation only.
notes: psbD has 74-nt and 47-nt 5'UTR forms; shorter form polysome-associated.

position_description: PRB1 at positions -14 to -11, complementary to the 3' end of 16S rRNA; changing GGAG->AAAG had no effect, GGAG->CCUC gave 4-fold lower D2 synthesis
experimental_evidence: site-directed mutagenesis + biolistic transformation; D2 synthesis/accumulation
key_finding: The psbD SD-like PRB1 (GGAG, -14/-11) contributes to but is not strictly required for translation; disruptive change reduces D2 ~4-fold.
notes: U-rich element at -20 to -15 described in same paper.

position_description: A highly U-rich sequence at positions -20 to -15 is required for translation; it serves as a molecular spacer between RNA-stabilization and translation elements
experimental_evidence: site-directed psbD leader mutants; in vitro UV cross-linking (40 kDa RBP); transgenic chloroplasts
key_finding: The psbD poly(U) element binds a 40-kDa Nac2-complex-associated protein and spaces stabilization vs translation cis-elements.

position_description: Three suppressor point mutations overcome loss of the U-rich element by disrupting a secondary structure that sequesters the psbD AUG in a double-stranded region
experimental_evidence: suppressor point mutations; site-directed chloroplast mutants; in vitro RNase H RNA mapping
key_finding: A psbD 5'UTR secondary structure occluding the AUG is a negative regulator enabling rapid shut-down of D2 synthesis.

position_description: nac2-26 mutant fails to accumulate the psbD transcript; NAC2 confers stability specifically on psbD mRNA
experimental_evidence: nuclear mutant characterization; transcript/protein analysis
key_finding: NAC2 is a nucleus-encoded trans-acting factor specifically required for psbD (D2) mRNA stability.
notes: Defines the NAC2 locus later used as a biotech regulatory switch.

position_description: Element I spans a maximum of 8 nt at the 5' end; forms a small stem-loop; essential for RNA stability and plays a role in translation
experimental_evidence: linker-scanning mutagenesis; in vitro nuclease mapping; in vivo DMS modification
key_finding: petD element I is a small 5' stem-loop blocking 5'->3' exonucleolytic decay (MCD1-dependent) and contributing to translation.

position_description: Element II (max 16 nt) in the center of the 5'UTR is essential for translation but not mRNA stability; no obvious secondary structure; protein-protected from DMS
experimental_evidence: linker-scanning mutagenesis; in vivo DMS footprint
key_finding: petD element II is a central protein-binding translation element independent of stability.

position_description: Element III (max 14 nt) near the 3' end of the 5'UTR forms a stem-loop in vivo; essential for translation; long-range interaction with element II
experimental_evidence: linker-scanning mutagenesis; intragenic suppressors; in vivo DMS
key_finding: petD element III is a stem-loop near the start codon required for translation via long-range RNA interaction with element II.

position_description: Two regions of the 362-nt 5'UTR act as positive translation elements: nt 150-200 and ~40 nt upstream of the start codon (~nt 320); SD-like element mutations tolerated
experimental_evidence: chloroplast transformation replacing WT petD 5'UTR with mutants
key_finding: petD translation depends on two positive 5'UTR regions; a putative SD element is dispensable; stability linked to translatability.

position_description: A transcriptional petD-uidA fusion makes mRNA but no translation; a translational fusion with the full petD 5'UTR gives high GUS; ~70% 5'UTR deletion lowers mRNA 4-6x and GUS 8x
experimental_evidence: transcriptional vs translational uidA fusions; run-on transcription
key_finding: Sequences essential for translation reside in the petD 5'UTR, which also affects mRNA stability; transcription rates equal across strains.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

position_description: Changing the petD initiation codon to AUU or AUC gives temperature-sensitive photosynthesis; subunit IV accumulation reduced to 10-20%; translation initiation inefficient
experimental_evidence: site-directed chloroplast mutagenesis; pulse labeling
key_finding: Non-AUG petD start codons impair translation initiation, causing ts photosynthetic growth.

position_description: Mutating the three nucleotides immediately upstream of the initiation codon (-1 triplet) caused ts translation decreases, worse when combined with an AUU start codon
experimental_evidence: site-directed mutagenesis of -1 triplet in two chloroplast genes in vivo
key_finding: An extended base-pairing interaction between the -1 triplet and the fMet-tRNA anticodon loop aids translation, compensating for lack of a classic SD interaction.
notes: Genes studied were atpB and petD per full text (abstract says 'two chloroplast genes').

position_description: Replacement mutagenesis eliminating SD complementarity, and insertion of a canonical SD (GGAGG) at positions -9 to -5, had no effect on aadA/uidA reporter expression in the chloroplast
sequence_source_location: abstract (canonical SD quoted; native SD-like sequences hypervariable, not quoted)
experimental_evidence: replacement mutagenesis; chloroplast and E. coli transformants; reporter assays
key_finding: SD-like sequences are NOT required for translation of most Chlamydomonas chloroplast mRNAs; plastids largely use SD-independent initiation.
notes: Contrasts with psbA/psbD where an SD-like element does contribute; dependence is gene-specific.

position_description: Mutations weakening stem structures in the rps7 5'UTR reduced reporter expression; compensatory second-site mutations restoring the second stem suppressed the defect
experimental_evidence: random + site-directed mutagenesis; chloroplast and E. coli reporters; UV melting; RNase T1
key_finding: A conserved rps7 5'UTR folding pattern (stem structures) is essential for translation initiation.

position_description: MCA1 acts on the very first 21 nt of the petA 5'UTR to protect the whole transcript from 5'->3' degradation; MCA1 and TCA1 recognize adjacent targets
experimental_evidence: chloroplast transformation with modified petA; cloning of MCA1 (PPR)
key_finding: MCA1 (a PPR protein) binds the extreme 5' end (first 21 nt) of petA mRNA to confer 5'->3' stability and assist TCA1-dependent translation.

position_description: TCA1 target site lies within the petA 5'UTR; a chloroplast suppressor placed petA coding under a duplicated heterologous 5'UTR
experimental_evidence: nuclear mutant genetics (21 alleles); chloroplast suppressor
key_finding: TCA1 is the sole nucleus-encoded translational activator for petA (cytochrome f), acting via the petA 5'UTR; mediates CES regulation.

position_description: Limiting MCA1 reduces petA mRNA; limiting TCA1 reduces cytochrome f translation; MCA1 is short-lived and responds to N availability and culture age
experimental_evidence: tagged factor dosage strains; physiological shifts
key_finding: Nucleus-encoded MCA1 and TCA1 are regulatory (not merely constitutive); their abundance sets petA mRNA and translation.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

position_description: Mbb1 target mapped to the psbB 5'UTR; psbB 5' ends at -147 (long) and -35 (short, WT-only); psbH has its own Mbb1 target
experimental_evidence: chimeric psbB::aadA chloroplast transformation; primer extension; poly(G) insertion
key_finding: The psbB/T/H cluster mRNAs require Mbb1 acting on 5'UTR cis-elements; 5'->3' exonuclease implicated; short psbB form is Mbb1-dependent.

position_description: A conserved cis-acting element at the 5' extremity of psbB and psbH 5'UTRs; two sRNAs correspond to the 5' ends of mature psbB and psbH mRNAs and are centered on these elements
experimental_evidence: small-RNA mining; chloroplast transformation + site-directed mutagenesis; in vitro RNA binding
key_finding: A conserved 5'UTR element bound by the TPR protein Mbb1 directs processing/stability and leaves protected sRNA footprints.

position_description: Mbb1 is a 662-aa stromal protein with 10 tetratricopeptide-like repeats, part of a 300-kDa RNA-associated complex
experimental_evidence: genomic rescue cloning; biochemical fractionation
key_finding: Mbb1 is a nucleus-encoded TPR protein required for psbB/T/H mRNA accumulation.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

position_description: The Tab2 target site is within the psaB 5'UTR; gel shift shows direct, specific Tab2-psaB 5'UTR interaction
experimental_evidence: nuclear mutant F14 genetics; genomic complementation; gel mobility shift; directed mutagenesis
key_finding: Tab2 is a conserved RNA-binding trans-factor required for psaB mRNA translation and PSI assembly, acting on the psaB 5'UTR.

position_description: TAA1 (OPR+RAP protein) is required for psaA mRNA stability and translation; TAA1 is down-regulated post-transcriptionally under iron limitation
experimental_evidence: nuclear mutant screen; localization; iron shift experiments
key_finding: TAA1 governs psaA (PsaA) expression and couples PSI accumulation to iron availability.

position_description: TDA1 (OPR protein, 8 repeats) is required for translation of atpA; a fraction of atpA transcripts is sequestered in non-polysomal RNP complexes
experimental_evidence: nuclear factor characterization; polysome/RNP fractionation
key_finding: TDA1 both traps and translationally activates atpA mRNA via the atpA 5'UTR.

position_description: MDA1 (OPR protein) binds a ~100-nt region in the middle of the atpA 5'UTR (same region as TDA1), governing maturation and accumulation
experimental_evidence: molecular identification of MDA1; binding; complex analysis
key_finding: MDA1 is an OPR stabilization factor binding mid-5'UTR (atypical, not the 5' end), forming a complex with TDA1 and atpA mRNA.

element_name: MDA1 acts on atpA coding region (dominant mutation)
position_description: The dominant mda1-ncc1 mutation affects atpA mRNA stability by acting on the coding region of the atpA transcript
experimental_evidence: nuclear mutant genetics; transcript analysis
key_finding: MDA1 influences atpA mRNA stability; a dominant allele implicates the coding region in the atpA stability pathway.

position_description: Point mutations in the 10-nt sequence at positions +38 to +47 shortened transcript longevity and reduced abundance >95%
experimental_evidence: point mutations in rbcL 5'UTR::uidA chimeras in vivo
key_finding: A specific 10-nt rbcL 5'UTR element (+38/+47), predicted part of an RNA secondary structure, is essential for transcript stability.

position_description: The 12-nt atpB 5'UTR sequence at positions +31 to +42 is important for transcript stability and accumulation
experimental_evidence: point mutations in atpB 5'UTR::uidA chimeras in vivo
key_finding: A specific 12-nt atpB 5'UTR element (+31/+42), predicted part of a secondary structure, stabilizes the transcript.

position_description: An essential 5' stem-loop mediates folding of a short sequence around its base into a specific helical+single-stranded conformation required for longevity; disrupting the fold destabilizes even with unchanged sequence
experimental_evidence: site-directed mutagenesis; RNase probing; in vivo decay
key_finding: The rbcL 5' stem-loop works by templating a specific downstream RNA conformation (not by simply blocking nucleases), presumably recognized by a trans-factor.

position_description: Changes at the beginning of the rbcL 5'UTR that affect RNA secondary structure make chimeric rbcL:GUS transcripts >50-fold less stable
experimental_evidence: deletion/mutational analysis; uidA reporters; in vivo
key_finding: rbcL 5'UTR secondary-structure changes accelerate degradation >50x, explaining apparent 'promoter' loss on 5'UTR deletion.
notes: Companion to Suay 2005 and Blowers/Klein promoter studies.

position_description: Extending the 5' terminus by >6 nt triggered rapid degradation; a poly(G) tract downstream of the 5' end blocked decay and trimmed 5' ends to the poly(G)
exact_sequence_if_reported: poly(G) tract (G-rich; exact length not specified in abstract)
experimental_evidence: uidA reporters flanked by rbcL 5'/psaB 3'; 5'-end mapping; poly(G) insertions
key_finding: Chloroplast mRNA degradation is initiated at the 5' end by a 5'->3' exoribonuclease, with sequence/condition-dependent (light-activated) modes.

position_description: Poly(G)18 insertions at -20/+25/+165 yielded mRNAs with 5' ends at the poly(G); interpreted as continuous 5'->3' exonucleolytic decay; -20 insertion suggests 5' maturation also uses this activity
experimental_evidence: poly(G)18 insertions in petD; WT vs mcd1; 5'-end analysis
key_finding: 5'->3' exoribonucleolytic activity is a normal petD decay pathway; MCD1 protects petD and may also be required for translation.

position_description: MCD1 is required for stability of petD mRNA; in mcd1, petD is degraded by 5'->3' exonuclease; MCD1 encodes a large novel protein
experimental_evidence: gene cloning; allele analysis; tRNA suppressor
key_finding: MCD1 is a nucleus-encoded petD-specific 5' stability factor.

position_description: mcd3/mcd4/mcd5 nuclear mutants (suppressors of petD 5' LS mutants) alter transcript patterns of up to 17 chloroplast genes, producing novel 3' ends
experimental_evidence: suppressor genetics; RNA filter hybridization of 32 genes
key_finding: MCD3-5 are pleiotropic nuclear factors participating in both 5' and 3' mRNA maturation/degradation; MCD4 interacts with MCD1.

position_description: A synthetic atpB precursor is cleaved ~10 nt downstream of the mature 3' end, then exonucleolytically trimmed; in vivo run-on shows <=50% of atpB transcripts terminate at/near the IR
experimental_evidence: in vitro processing of synthetic precursor; in vivo run-on; chimeric atpB transformants
key_finding: atpB 3'-end maturation is a two-step endonucleolytic cleavage + 3'->5' trimming; the 3' IR is only a partial (<=50%) terminator.

position_description: Deleting part/all of the 3' stem/loop reduced atpB mRNA to 20-35% of WT with heterogeneous sizes, while transcription rates were unaffected
experimental_evidence: deletions in transformed cells; RNA blots; transcription rates
key_finding: The atpB 3' stem/loop functions in both mRNA stabilization and 3'-end formation, not transcription termination.

position_description: Chimeric GUS genes fused to rbcL or psaB 3' IRs in forward orientation accumulated a single transcript size; without an IR, heterogeneous sizes accumulated
experimental_evidence: chimeric atpB promoter::GUS with 3' IR variants; chloroplast transformation
key_finding: The rbcL and psaB 3' flanking IRs define the 3' terminus of a transcript in vivo (processing/stability signal).

position_description: Synthetic atpB and petD 3'UTR RNAs gave stable processing products in chloroplast extract; petA and antisense atpB 3'UTR were degraded; in vivo antisense 3'UTRs halved discrete mRNA
experimental_evidence: in vitro processing in chloroplast extract; in vivo 3'UTR swaps (sense/antisense)
key_finding: Both the nucleotide sequence and the stem-loop structure of 3'UTRs matter for 3' processing and mature-mRNA accumulation; IRs are not transcription terminators.

position_description: Mutants lacking the 3' stem-loop showed 75% lower psaB mRNA and faster decay; extending the ORF into the IR cut mRNA to 2% of WT
experimental_evidence: site-directed chloroplast mutants; pulse-chase mRNA decay
key_finding: The psaB 3' stem-loop is required for mRNA stability; ribosome intrusion into the stem-loop strongly destabilizes; both UAG and UGA terminate translation in vivo.

position_description: Strains with the atpB 3' IR deleted are weakly phototrophic; 18 guanosine residues substitute for the IR in vivo, restoring near-WT atpB transcripts/protein; poly(G) is not a terminator
experimental_evidence: chloroplast transformation; transcript/protein analysis
key_finding: atpB transcripts lacking the 3' IR are degraded by 3'->5' exoribonuclease; a poly(G)18 block substitutes functionally, proving the IR is a stability/anti-exonuclease element.

position_description: A cis-element in the center of the second inverted repeat (IR2) is required for 3' processing; deleting IR1 or IR2 alone still allows stable mRNA, but deleting both abolishes rbcL mRNA
experimental_evidence: insertional reporter screen in tscA; chloroplast suppressors; 3'UTR mutations
key_finding: The two rbcL 3' inverted repeats act as redundant mRNA-stability determinants; IR2 contains a processing cis-element.

position_description: atpA and psbD 5'UTRs (incl. promoter) gave the highest chimeric mRNA and protein; rbcL and psbA 5'UTRs gave less; varying the 3'UTR had little effect as long as one was present
experimental_evidence: heterologous gfp reporter fused combinatorially to 5' and 3' UTRs; chloroplast transformation
key_finding: Benchmark comparison of Chlamydomonas chloroplast 5'/3'UTRs for transgene expression; atpA/psbD 5'UTRs are strongest; light-regulated translation persists for psbA/psbD.
notes: Widely cited parts benchmark (the requested Barnes et al. 2005).

position_description: Fusing the strong 16S rRNA promoter to the psbA or atpA 5'UTR; 16S/psbA had little extra effect in a psbA-deficient background (psbA/D1 auto-attenuation)
experimental_evidence: chloroplast transformation; reporter accumulation
key_finding: Promoter/5'UTR engineering: the 16S promoter + atpA 5'UTR is a strong constitutive cassette; psbA 5'UTR needs a psbA-deficient background due to D1 autoregulation.
notes: Volume/pages verified via Europe PMC; the requested Rasala et al. 2011.

position_description: Seven human therapeutic proteins expressed from chloroplast cassettes; >50% expressed, three at 2-3% of total soluble protein
experimental_evidence: chloroplast transformation; protein accumulation/bioactivity assays
key_finding: Demonstrates Chlamydomonas chloroplast regulatory cassettes support commercial-scale heterologous protein accumulation.

position_description: Hundreds of designed variants of endogenous 5'UTRs (incl. psbD) screened in vivo; essential regions identified by deep sequencing of thousands of mutants
experimental_evidence: arrayed oligonucleotide 5'UTR library; chloroplast transformation; NGS of mutants
key_finding: High-throughput synthetic-biology dissection of chloroplast 5'UTRs validates and refines essential psbD translational elements for part design.
notes: Volume/pages verified via Europe PMC (ACS Synth Biol 2:34-46); the requested Specht & Mayfield.

position_description: New marker-recycling vectors and a psaA-based host enabled synthesis of human growth hormone in C. reinhardtii chloroplast
experimental_evidence: chloroplast transformation; protein expression
key_finding: Provides improved endogenous promoter/UTR vectors and a robust expression host for secreted/therapeutic proteins.
notes: Volume/pages verified via Europe PMC (Appl Microbiol Biotechnol 100:5467-5477).

position_description: Fusion immunotoxins (antibody + toxin) produced in the chloroplast using endogenous psbA/atpA regulatory elements
experimental_evidence: chloroplast transformation; protein accumulation/activity
key_finding: Shows endogenous chloroplast UTRs support expression of complex multidomain therapeutic proteins impossible in E. coli.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

position_description: Over 140 regulatory parts (native and synthetic promoters, 5'/3'UTRs, intercistronic expression elements) characterized; library-based synthetic promoter design
experimental_evidence: automated transplastomic strain generation; reporter quantification
key_finding: Largest systematic characterization of Chlamydomonas chloroplast regulatory parts, enabling predictable part choice and synthetic promoter design.
notes: Recent; strong resource for a comparative parts table.

position_description: BDP1 (atpA/rbcL IR) drives two transgenes in opposing orientations; methyl-jasmonate selectively enhances BDP1 output; BDP3 (psbH/psbN) minimal (UTR-dependent)
experimental_evidence: comparative conservation analysis (15 species); semi-rational screen; fluorescent reporters
key_finding: Natural chloroplast bidirectional intergenic promoters are functional multigene-engineering tools; conservation varies across microalgae/plants.
notes: Also relevant comparative-genomics precedent for this project.

position_description: Tobacco PrbcL and PpsbA promoters did NOT effectively drive expression in Chlamydomonas chloroplast; tobacco terminators TrbcL/Trps16 worked; Cr-IEE5 strongly affected downstream expression
experimental_evidence: chloroplast transformation; NanoLuc reporter
key_finding: Land-plant chloroplast promoters are largely non-portable to Chlamydomonas, whereas terminators and some IEEs transfer; guides heterologous-part choice.

position_description: Golden Gate (MoClo) collection of standardized chloroplast promoters, terminators, reporter and selection parts in vector pWF.K.4 (petA integration site)
experimental_evidence: Golden Gate assembly; multigene chloroplast transformation; expression assays
key_finding: Provides a standardized, syntax-compatible part toolkit for Chlamydomonas chloroplast engineering.

position_description: Identification and characterization of endogenous promoters and homologous targeting regions to build H. pluvialis chloroplast transformation vectors
experimental_evidence: chloroplast genome characterization; vector construction
key_finding: First development of chloroplast genetic tools (endogenous regulatory + targeting regions) for H. pluvialis, a non-Chlamydomonas green alga.
notes: Main primary example of endogenous chloroplast regulatory-region work outside Chlamydomonas among green algae; no PMCID (abstract only).
